questions.q: Why can't docker compose up spread Northbridge's catalog, api, and db services across multiple hosts?
options: Compose's model assumes every service runs on the same machine -- it has no concept of scheduling containers across hosts
Compose can already do this with the --multi-host flag
Docker images can only ever run on the host that built them
Postgres specifically refuses to run on more than one host
questions.explain: Compose was designed to manage containers on one host -- its shared network, volumes, and depends_on are all scoped to that single machine, with no built-in way to span multiple hosts.

questions.q: What does "scheduling" mean in the context of a container orchestrator?
options: Setting a cron job inside a container
Deciding which of many available hosts should run a given container, based on resources
Configuring a HEALTHCHECK's --interval
Automatically writing a compose.yaml file
questions.explain: Scheduling is the orchestrator's job of deciding, across a cluster of hosts, where each container actually runs.

questions.q: What does "self-healing" add beyond what a restart policy (Lesson 25) already provides on one host?
options: Nothing -- they are exactly the same feature with a different name
It extends automatic recovery to the cluster level -- rescheduling a container elsewhere if the entire host it was running on goes down
It automatically fixes bugs in the application's source code
It only applies to database containers, never to stateless services
questions.explain: A restart policy recovers a crashed container on the same host. Self-healing at the cluster level goes further, rescheduling containers if an entire host fails.

options: A monitoring dashboard for docker stats
Docker's own built-in orchestrator, which can turn a compose.yaml's deploy: block into a real multi-host deployment
A third-party replacement for the docker CLI
A Docker Hub feature for hosting private images
questions.explain: Docker Swarm is Docker's native orchestrator, using much of the same compose.yaml syntax (including the deploy: block) to run services across multiple hosts.

questions.q: What is Kubernetes, relative to Docker Swarm?
options: A competing container runtime that replaces Docker entirely
The industry-standard orchestrator solving the same core problems as Swarm -- scheduling, self-healing, scaling -- with its own YAML shapes and a much larger ecosystem
A Docker Desktop feature that is identical in every way to Swarm
A logging driver, like json-file or local
questions.explain: Kubernetes addresses the same orchestration problems as Swarm but with its own object model (Pods, Deployments, Services) and is the more widely adopted choice in production.
